entities.name: presynaptic GABAA receptors on primary afferent terminals
early RET+ dorsal horn inhibitory neurons

relationships.subject: NKCC1
relationships.evidence_quote: This is caused by the high expression of the transporter NKCC1 (transporting Cl−, Na+ and K+ into the cell) and the low, or even undetectable, expression of KCC2

relationships.subject: presynaptic GABAA receptors on primary afferent terminals
relationships.evidence_quote: Presynaptic GABAARs expressed on PAF terminals mediate primary afferent depolarization (PAD) in spinal cord dorsal horn

relationships.subject: primary afferent depolarization
relationships.evidence_quote: In physiological conditions, PAD exerts an inhibitory effect on glutamate release, through several possible mechanisms

relationships.subject: presynaptic GABAA receptors on primary afferent terminals
relationships.evidence_quote: GABA, released after the first pulse, acts on presynaptic GABAARs, reducing glutamate release from Aβ fibers at the second stimulus

relationships.subject: presynaptic GABAB receptors
relationships.evidence_quote: presynaptic GABABRs inhibit pinch- and touch-evoked synaptic responses in vivo [42] and decrease glutamate and peptide release from A- and C-type PAFs and dorsal horn neurons

relationships.subject: dorsal horn PV+ interneurons
relationships.evidence_quote: opto-stimulation of PV+ neurons prior to dorsal root electrical stimulation causes a time-dependent reduction of the amplitude of evoked EPSCs recorded from dorsal horn neurons, confirming the involvement of PV+ neurons in presynaptic inhibition

relationships.subject: early RET+ dorsal horn inhibitory neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: their optogenetic activation inhibits Aβ or C fiber-mediated responses in dorsal horn neurons, through the activation of presynaptic GABAB receptors

relationships.subject: RVM GABAergic/enkephalinergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Ablation of GABAergic/enkephalinergic RVM neurons, by using a Cre-dependent active caspase system, causes hypersensitivity to both heat and mechanical stimuli, whereas chemogenetic activation of these neurons produces antinociception

key_findings: Review: high NKCC1 and low KCC2 in primary sensory neurons set ECl near -30 mV, so presynaptic GABAA receptor activation depolarizes afferent terminals (PAD) and inhibits glutamate release.

Presynaptic GABAA (phasic) and tonically active GABAB receptors on Abeta afferent terminals limit transmitter release; PV+, early RET+ interneurons and descending RVM GABAergic fibers mediate presynaptic inhibition.
